\section{Use finiteness to recover an invariant predecessor}

\subsection{The generic mathematical principle}

Let \(A\) be finite, \(f:A\to A\) injective, and \(P\) a forward-invariant predicate:
\[
 P(x)\Longrightarrow P(f(x)).
\]
The restriction of \(f\) to \(\{x:P(x)\}\) is an injection from a finite set to itself, hence is surjective. Therefore \(P(f(x))\Rightarrow P(x)\). More usefully, every point satisfying \(P\) has a predecessor satisfying \(P\).

Mathlib already packages the required result in
\code{Set.Finite.injOn_iff_bijOn_of_mapsTo}; see
\mathsrc{Data/Set/Finite/Basic}{restricted injections and bijections}. The production patch uses this theorem directly, so no extra generic helper has to be added to the library.

\subsection{Application to the offset-19 exclusion}

The target is \src{NativeFieldCycles2011}{65--91}. After the existing argument identifies the exceptional source value as 511, put
\[
 P(i)\ :\!\iff\ S(i)\equiv0\pmod2.
\]
The existing \code{successor_mod_four} implies forward invariance of \(P\). The proposed proof restricts the given finite permutation to the even-value subset and obtains a predecessor \(j\) of the allegedly 510-valued point \(i\), with \(S(j)\) even. Applying \code{successor_mod_four} to \(j\) yields \(S(i)\equiv0\pmod4\), contradicting \(510\equiv2\pmod4\).

The current proof obtains the same predecessor indirectly: it proves evenness along all iterates, finds a positive period, constructs the iterate at period minus one, and proves that one successor returns to the starting point. None of that orbit arithmetic is required once restricted surjectivity is available.

The complete file shrinks from \textbf{111 to 104 lines}. Its periodic-points import is replaced by the finite-set API import. Both complete versions compile, public theorem statements agree, and the audited axiom sets agree.

\textbf{Sharp limits.} The finite and injective hypotheses are essential to the generic reflection principle. Successor on the infinite natural numbers preserves positivity but does not reflect it at zero. A noninjective map on a finite set can enter an invariant subset from outside. The patch retains all needed assumptions. It also leaves the legitimate 511 self-loop and the separate offset-20 theorem unchanged; the latter still needs no finiteness or permutation hypothesis.

## Provisional gaps worth checking in maintained sources

The two packets are concentrated on representation layouts, scanners, DAG certificates, native field/carry geometry and object-model administration. They do not specifically analyze (a) proof by uniqueness of functional arithmetic graphs to eliminate repeated existential witnesses; (b) reconstruction/projection equivalences for split encodings beyond ordinary witness concatenation; (c) deriving feasibility/zero-set equivalence endpoints by relation algebra rather than fresh bidirectional witness proofs; (d) generic natural-difference bounds or order embeddings used outside the discussed cyclic field geometry; or (e) specialized induction principles for syntax-recursive pair encodings. These are search directions, not verified proposals or novelty claims. Every chosen concrete implementation still needs comparison with the exclusion matrix and its actual upstream source.

/-- Quotienting a cyclic word by its cell length is a ring homomorphism. -/
def residue {N L : ℕ} : ZMod (N * L) →+* ZMod L :=
  ZMod.castHom (Nat.dvd_mul_left L N) (ZMod L)

theorem residue_val {N L : ℕ} [NeZero (N * L)] (k : ZMod (N * L)) :
    (residue k).val = k.val % L := by
  simp only [residue, ZMod.castHom_apply, ZMod.cast_eq_val, ZMod.val_natCast]

\section{D: separate supports through a quotient homomorphism}\label{sec:support}

\subsection{A reusable mathematical statement}

Let \(G,H\) be additive commutative groups, \(\pi:G\to H\) an additive homomorphism, \(S\subseteq H\), and \(t\in G\). Suppose the function \(f\) has support contained in the translated preimage of \(S\):
\[
 \pi(x-t)\notin S\ \Longrightarrow\ f(x)=0.
\]
Define
\[
 S-S=\{b-a:a,b\in S\}.
\]
If \(y=x+\delta\) and \(\pi(\delta)\notin S-S\), then
\[
 f(x)=0\quad\lor\quad f(y)=0.
\]
Indeed, if both values were nonzero, both projected locations would belong to \(S\), and their difference would be
\[
 \pi(y-t)-\pi(x-t)=\pi(y-x)=\pi(\delta),
\]
contradicting the excluded difference. The common translation cancels in the group before any natural-number remainder reasoning is performed.

\subsection{The actual native client}

The checked application uses the quotient
\[
 \Z/(4831N)\Z\longrightarrow\Z/4831\Z
\]
and the coarse support
\[
 S=\{j:j.\mathrm{val}\le583\ \lor\ j.\mathrm{val}=1203\ \lor\ j.\mathrm{val}=1807\}.
\]
The exact displacement certificate is \(606\notin S-S\). Applying the generic theorem to the temporal rotation produces the original conclusion of
\code{NativeTemporalSupport54.clause_pair_one_zero}. The full temporal shift remains in the ambient cyclic group; only the support test is projected to the cell quotient.

The source already proves a natural-number \code{no_difference_606} obstruction. Its discovery is not new. The contribution here is the projected group interface that packages this obstruction and removes repeated translation/residue bookkeeping from prospective clients.

\subsection{When to adopt it}

The generic theorem, the modular certificate, and the complete native module compile. The existing public theorem header is unchanged. However, counting the helper increases the source from 82 to 125 physical lines and from 4,190 to 5,499 bytes. The candidate is therefore best retained until a second or third support-separation theorem can reuse it. If there is only this client, the existing direct proof is smaller.

\section{One finite-fiber identity for folded stencils}

\src{NativeCyclicConvolution} proves \code{mass_foldStencil},
\code{convolution_foldStencil}, and the finite-sum step inside
\code{word_foldStencil} by repeatedly swapping sums and collapsing an equality
filter. All are instances of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pushforward}
 \sum_{k\in K}\left(\sum_{i\in I:p(i)=k}a_i\right)w_k
 =\sum_{i\in I}a_iw_{p(i)}.
\end{equation}
The supplied \code{FinitePushforward.sum_fiber_mul} proves this for finite
index types, an arbitrary map $p:I\to K$, and a semiring. Multiplication need
not be commutative, because the order $a_iw_{p(i)}$ is retained. Decidable
equality on $K$ is used to express the finite filter.

Three specializations are immediate: $w_k=1$ for mass,
$w_k=c(q-k)$ for convolution at $q$, and $w_k=\rho^{\operatorname{val}(k)}$
for a word. For the last specialization, the existing
\code{pow_mod_length} argument is still required to replace the reduced
exponent by the original exponent modulo $\rho^n-1$.

\checked: the generic identity compiles. It assumes no injectivity of $p$,
so all collisions are retained. It does not establish no-carry bounds, mask
compatibility, or uniqueness of a word representation. A safe integration
replaces the repeated finite-sum rearrangement and preserves those separate
arithmetic obligations.

This is a useful example of a small abstraction with several interpretations.
It makes the collision behavior obvious at the interface instead of requiring
each proof reader to reconstruct it from a double sum.
